auditor.notes: Isolated re-audit (revision_round 2) replacing the round-1 audit. The round-1 audit was a same_session_late_pass run inside the planner conversation and self-certified planner_conversation_isolated=true; an in-conversation audit cannot self-certify isolation, and the plan-auditor skill's independence requirement does not permit it — the round-1 record is superseded as invalid for that reason. This pass ran as a fresh subagent that never saw the planning conversation; inputs were the plan directory (artifacts only), the stage-0 snapshot, read-only spot checks of snapshot-listed files, the stage-1 frozen baseline named by the task as the baseline, and the README platform note the plan's A-2 rationale cites. Every check below was performed from the artifacts; no planner-conversation reasoning was available to reuse.

grounding.notes: Frozen-item drift judgment (this probe's core question): (1) C1 carry-forward — the stage-2 C1 spec is RAW byte-identical to the stage-1 C1 spec (programmatic comparison, not strip-only), with identical unfreeze_rule and logical_owner: the frozen GET /todos API shape is unchanged, no silent drift. (2) C2 carry-forward — the stage-2 C2 is a pure additive: ', webhook_url?: string' inserted after 'tag?: string' with existing keys and their order preserved, plus an in-writing proposal note recorded in the spec per C2's unfreeze rule ('additive-only until stage 2 proposes otherwise in writing'); last_notified_at deliberately NOT added. (3) The product ticket note (last_notified_at in GET /todos) is NOT absorbed: out_of_scope with rule-based reason (a ticket note is input to a formal contract change request, not the request itself C1's unfreeze rule requires), recorded as non-blocking open question Q1 (owner: user), with a conditional forecast stage that depends on the Q1 decision and a C1 revision — matching the README platform note ('any change to a frozen item is drift and must be surfaced, not absorbed silently') and the stage-1 checkpoint's downstream_notes. (4) app/webhooks.py: WebhookDispatcher.send appends to WebhookLog.sent and returns 200, never raises by design — A-2 is a verified repo fact, and the reuse constraint (no new HTTP client/worker/queue) is feasible without modifying the dispatcher. (5) tests/test_api.py::test_create_and_list_shape asserts the exact per-todo key set {id,title,done} — the C1 canary named in A4 exists in the frozen suite. (6) mark_done (app/api.py) re-applies done=true and returns 200 even for an already-done todo (idempotent) — the repo basis for finding F01. (7) stage-1 out-of-scope items (multi-user auth, bulk operations) are carried into stage-2 out_of_scope, and the stage-1 forecast objective ('stage 2: notifications on completion') is met by the stage-2 objective. (8) Inlined frozen contracts: all 7 inlined specs in tasks/T01.json, T02.json, T03.json match the current stage-contract specs byte-for-byte and by sha256 source_hash (programmatic verification). No repo drift observed: the four snapshot-listed files match the snapshot's layer/import map; stage-1/ files and README.md are outside the scan boundary (snapshot unknown_areas) and were read as the task-named frozen baseline and as the platform note the plan cites, not as a repo re-scan.

findings.evidence: app/api.py mark_done re-applies todo['done']=True and returns 200 even when the todo is already done, so a repeated done is a 'successful' call in the repo's own semantics. C3 says 'on a successful mark_done (todo exists, transition applied), exactly one webhook is dispatched' — the parenthetical does not settle whether a repeat done (state unchanged) counts as a transition applied, and A1.negative_case ('marking the same todo done again is a no-op state-wise but still returns 200 (idempotent transition)') is silent on the dispatch count. An executor therefore must decide whether a second done logs a second webhook for the same todo.done event (duplicates) or zero (one notification per completion event); the product reading favors the latter, but no acceptance test pins it.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin it in one place: state in C3 (or A1.negative_case) that a repeat done on an already-done todo dispatches zero webhooks (WebhookLog.sent count stays 1), and add the assertion-level case to tests/test_notifications.py (mark a done todo done again; assert WebhookLog.sent still has exactly 1 entry).

findings.evidence: T03's e2e test file must import app/api.py (TodoAPI under test) and app/webhooks.py (WebhookDispatcher — the E2 raising-dispatcher scenario has to construct a dispatcher whose send() raises), and asserts on store records (app/store.py), yet tasks/T03.json required_context.files lists only tests/test_api.py and the new tests/test_e2e_notifications.py. A fresh executor loading exactly the declared context would have to discover the production modules on its own (possible — the declared frozen suite imports them — but the context closure is not fully declared).
findings.suggested_fix: Add app/api.py, app/webhooks.py, and app/store.py to T03.required_context.files (read-only; T03's owned_paths stays test-only).

findings.evidence: plan-check.py validate run-manifest.json (schema planning/run-manifest@1) fails: missing required top-level keys plan_id, stage_id, created_at, audit_verdict; every pipeline row missing required status and gate; every gate row missing required name; pipeline[].stage is int where the schema expects string. The manifest is a gate/attribution log, not an execution input, so this does not block execution — but an artifact that declares a schema must validate against it, and plan-check lint does not cover this file (lint passed 0/0/0 while the manifest is schema-invalid).
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite run-manifest.json to the run-manifest@1 shape (add plan_id, stage_id, created_at, audit_verdict; per-row status + gate; per-gate name; string stage ids), or drop the schema declaration if the manifest is meant to be freeform. Re-validate after.
